properties.label: Labels
properties.description: Labels pair a product area (where in Q-DO the problem or request is) with an issue type (bug, feature request, documentation, how-to), plus three standalone labels. Apply a label for every distinct problem or request the customer raises anywhere in the conversation, including follow-ups; one problem gets one label.
properties.instructions: Which Q-DO product area and issue type labels apply to the problems or requests the customer raises in this support conversation?

optionDescriptions.TASKS_LISTS_BUG: TASKS_LISTS_BUG: something that exists in Q-DO doesn't work as it should, such as data not saved, garbled or lost, wrong behavior, sync failures, crashes, installs or sign-ins that fail, or a device that should be supported being refused. Area: creating and editing tasks and lists on the customer's own account: task titles, notes, subtasks, priorities, due dates, recurring tasks, completion, reminders and notifications, list order, sorting, progress, pinning, and organizing lists (folders, tags, templates, views). Help questions about Q-DO in general also go here.
optionDescriptions.TASKS_LISTS_FEATURE_REQUEST: TASKS_LISTS_FEATURE_REQUEST: the customer asks for something Q-DO doesn't do, even if phrased as a complaint ("why can't I..."), including support for a device, OS or browser Q-DO doesn't support. Area: creating and editing tasks and lists on the customer's own account: task titles, notes, subtasks, priorities, due dates, recurring tasks, completion, reminders and notifications, list order, sorting, progress, pinning, and organizing lists (folders, tags, templates, views). Help questions about Q-DO in general also go here.
optionDescriptions.TASKS_LISTS_DOCUMENTATION: TASKS_LISTS_DOCUMENTATION: the customer looked for help and the help center, FAQ or in-app guidance is missing, unclear, wrong, outdated or mistranslated, while the product itself works. Area: creating and editing tasks and lists on the customer's own account: task titles, notes, subtasks, priorities, due dates, recurring tasks, completion, reminders and notifications, list order, sorting, progress, pinning, and organizing lists (folders, tags, templates, views). Help questions about Q-DO in general also go here.
optionDescriptions.TASKS_LISTS_HOW_TO: TASKS_LISTS_HOW_TO: the customer asks how to do something or for advice on using Q-DO, without pointing to a documentation problem and with nothing broken. Area: creating and editing tasks and lists on the customer's own account: task titles, notes, subtasks, priorities, due dates, recurring tasks, completion, reminders and notifications, list order, sorting, progress, pinning, and organizing lists (folders, tags, templates, views). Help questions about Q-DO in general also go here.
optionDescriptions.SYNC_BUG: SYNC_BUG: something that exists in Q-DO doesn't work as it should, such as data not saved, garbled or lost, wrong behavior, sync failures, crashes, installs or sign-ins that fail, or a device that should be supported being refused. Area: keeping one person's own devices in step: changes, checkmarks or lists that differ between their devices, offline changes that don't upload, and sync-conflict prompts. Problems between different people on a shared list are sharing, not sync.

properties.label: Urgency
properties.description: Urgency reflects the impact of the problem as the customer reports it, graded on the most urgent problem in the conversation. Do not lower it because support later answered, worked around or fixed it. Feature requests are LOW unless something is actually broken; if impact is unclear, choose MEDIUM for bugs and LOW for everything else.
properties.instructions: How urgent is the customer's problem in this Q-DO support conversation, judged by how much it hurts them and how soon support must act?

optionDescriptions.HIGH: Must be addressed immediately. The customer cannot use Q-DO at all, or faces loss, exposure or lockout: can't sign in or reach their account, can't create an account at all, sees another person's data, the app won't install, start or stay open on any device they use, a service outage, or tasks or lists permanently lost.
optionDescriptions.MEDIUM: Should be addressed soon. Something is broken and gets in the way, but Q-DO is still usable: a bug blocking a non-critical feature (export, print, reminders, archive view), intermittent or partial sync problems, slow shared-list changes, edits that sometimes don't save, crashes limited to one device or one large list, a failing invite, or a bug with a known workaround. Also a LOW problem the customer says blocks a deadline or their whole team.
optionDescriptions.LOW: Can be addressed later. Nothing important is broken: cosmetic bugs, feature requests, general feedback, documentation gaps, how-to and advice questions, and messages that are not support requests or ask for nothing.

properties.label: Sentiment
properties.description: Sentiment is the emotion the customer (not support) expresses, not the severity of the problem; a calm report of a serious bug is neutral. Consider all customer messages but weight the latest most, since it shows how the customer feels now. With no clear emotional signal, choose neutral.
properties.instructions: What is the customer's sentiment in this Q-DO support conversation, weighting their most recent message most heavily?

optionDescriptions.unhappy: Clear frustration or disappointment: words like "frustrating", "annoying", "disappointed", "this is the third time", saying the problem blocks their work, or impatient follow-ups. Also when a polite customer's latest message says the problem still isn't fixed and expresses frustration.
optionDescriptions.neutral: Matter-of-fact: reports a problem, asks a question or makes a request in polite but unemotional language. Routine courtesies like "Hi" or "Thanks" alone do not make it positive.
optionDescriptions.happy: Positive: appreciation, satisfaction with the answer or fix, or affection for the product, with little or no frustration. Also when the latest message says the problem is fixed and thanks support, even if the customer started frustrated.
